what: Every published entity's NAME, set in every script this archive can honestly write, and refused by name in the one it cannot. The owner's instruction of 3 September 2026: a character page should show the name in tengwar, cirth and sarati, as Tolkien Gateway does.
not_from_tolkien_gateway: TOLKIEN GATEWAY HAS NO TRANSCRIPTION TO TAKE. Its tengwar are IMAGES and MediaWiki templates, not text, so nothing here could have been scraped from it even if the archive wished to. Every glyph below is DERIVED by this archive from Appendix E through its own published letter tables.
hand_ruling: A TRANSCRIPTION THIS ARCHIVE COMPUTES IS THIS ARCHIVE'S OWN WORK AND NOT TOLKIEN'S. Every row names its mode, its rule-source and whether the mode is the name's own tongue's or was APPLIED. Publishing a computed transcription as though attested is the false-citation class C865 and C869 exist against, and nothing here is offered as attested.
reads: site/arda_codex_manifest.json (the routes) · site/arda_scripts.json and site/arda_tengwar_mode_q.json (the tengwar) · site/arda_cirth.json and site/arda_cirth_codepoints.json (the cirth) · site/arda_eldamo_lexicon.json (the language attribution) · site/arda_genealogy.json and site/arda_chronology.json (the names). NO LETTER VALUE IS RESTATED HERE.
transcribers: map/gen_tengwar.transcribe (Quenya, classical), map/gen_tengwar_mode_gu.transcribe (General Use) and map/gen_edge_scripts.cirth_transcribe. IMPORTED, never reimplemented: a second transcriber is a second answer, and this dataset and site/arda_edge_scripts.json would drift apart on a letter with nothing to notice it.
denominator: every route in site/arda_codex_manifest.json whose entityType is person, place or realm

modes_refused.the Mode of Beleriand: STILL REFUSED, and unchanged by C896. Appendix E describes it and never states its vowel values; site/arda_cirth.json refuses them by name. A Sindarin name is therefore not set in the tengwar AS SINDARIN. It goes to the Angerthas, which Appendix E does assign to it, and to the General Use, which DTS 58 states is 'applicable to both S[indarin] and Q[uenya]' -- and the row says which of the two it is in `basis`.
modes_refused.the General Use: NO LONGER REFUSED, and this entry stays to record that it WAS. Under his ruling C896 of 6 September 2026 Appendix E's plate was read by hand for the General Use and the reading is published in site/arda_tengwar_mode_gu.json, [I-H] on every row. The refusal it replaces read 'per-letter consonant assignments UNESTABLISHED ... every source renders that chart as an image', and its supporting measurement -- that the phrase 'general use' occurs ZERO times in The Lord of the Rings -- was TRUE and measured the wrong thing: Appendix E never uses the phrase and states the general application of the series and grades in prose regardless. What is still refused is refused by NUMBER in that file: tengwar 19, 20, 23 and 24 have no general-use value in Appendix E's prose.
modes_refused.every sarati mode: REFUSED, and not for want of a font or of permission. The archive holds 48/48 of the CSUR sarati block in fonts/ArdaCSUR.woff2, Bjorkman's outline face fonts/TirionSarati.woff2, and 66 value-labelled plates in site/sarati/ -- and NOTHING JOINS A SHAPE TO A SOUND. site/arda_sarati_keyboard.json refuses `sound -> glyph` and `sound -> codepoint` in its own words; reports/sarati_findings.json records zero assertable values; docs/sarati_values.md records that every value table in every reachable source is an IMAGE carrying no text. site/arda_sarati_tirion.json -- the shape-matching bridge that would supply it -- has never been written. A sarat can be DRAWN here and cannot be READ, so no name is set in it. CLAUDE.md section 6: a font is not a mapping.

sarati_would_settle_it: Either the ConScript Registry's own Sarati chart (codepoint -> name), which 14 fetch attempts have not reached, or Unifont's upstream .hex source for U+E390-E3BF if its entries carry semantic names -- with the 66 plate labels as the falsification test, not as the answer.

font_finding.what: TengwarTelcontar.woff2 AND Eldamar-1.1.woff2 DRAW TENGWAR AT THE CIRTH CODEPOINTS. Measured 3 September 2026 with fontTools against the faces this repository publishes.
font_finding.evidence: TengwarTelcontar maps U+E080..U+E08B to glyphs named TINCO, PARMA, CALMA, QUESSE, ANDO, UMBAR, ANGA, UNGWE, THUULE, FORMEN, HARMA, HWESTA -- Appendix E's tengwar 1-12, IN ORDER, at the ConScript *cirth* codepoints. Their outlines carry 52-76 curve segments against 1-5 straight ones; a certh is an angular rune and has no curve in it. Eldamar-1.1's U+E080 block has the same signature. ArdaCSUR rasterised at 16x16 gives stems with angular branches -- the Angerthas.
font_finding.why_it_hid: CMAP COVERAGE WAS THE PROXY AND IT IS NOT THE PROPERTY. Every one of those faces 'covers' U+E080-U+E0FF, and a coverage count is what was measured. What a codepoint DRAWS was never asked.
font_finding.this_dataset: cirth is set in fonts/ArdaCSUR.woff2 alone. A coarse certh is right; a crisp tengwa is wrong.
font_finding.elsewhere_and_not_fixed_here: THE SAME SUBSTITUTION IS LIVE IN THE PUBLISHED FORE-EDGE BAND. Measured across site/arda_edge_scripts.json: 31,213 of 49,683 certh glyph occurrences (62.8%) fall to Eldamar or TengwarTelcontar under codex-object.css's stack, on 1,354 of 1,354 cirth leaves. It is NOT repaired here because that stack lives in site/codex-object.css, which is extracted verbatim from site/codex-proto.html -- the one file nobody may edit without the owner naming the change. Reported, priced, and left for him.

language_cite.eldamo: Eldamo, Paul Strack, CC BY 4.0 -- site/arda_eldamo_lexicon.json. [EXT]: a scholar's attribution, and it chooses a MODE here, never a fact about Arda.
language_cite.not-established: Eldamo records no form matching this name, so no tongue is claimed for it and any mode applied to it is declared as the archive's own.

rule_source.tengwar: site/arda_tengwar_mode_q.json and site/arda_scripts.json -- the letter values are READ there and are not restated here. Encoding: ConScript Unicode Registry tengwar, U+E000-U+E07F. Faces: fonts/Eldamar-1.1.woff2, then fonts/TengwarTelcontar.woff2 and fonts/AlcarinTengwar-Regular.woff2 -- all CSUR-encoded, all with a recorded licence in site/arda_assets.json
rule_source.tengwar-gu: site/arda_tengwar_mode_gu.json -- THE GENERAL USE, published under his ruling C896 of 6 September 2026. Appendix E's plate read by hand: the plate gives the shape and the number, Appendix E's prose gives the value at that number, and every row is [I-H] with the sentence it was read from quoted beside it and re-verified through map/ardatext.py on every build. 29 sounds set, 7 tengwar refused BY NUMBER, 4 spellings refused BY NAME. The Series III/IV assignment is the one Appendix E states for 'languages like the Westron'. Encoding: ConScript Unicode Registry tengwar, U+E000-U+E07F. Faces: fonts/Eldamar-1.1.woff2, then fonts/TengwarTelcontar.woff2 and fonts/AlcarinTengwar-Regular.woff2 -- all CSUR-encoded, all with a recorded licence in site/arda_assets.json
rule_source.cirth: site/arda_cirth.json for the letter VALUES, each carrying its own marker; site/arda_cirth_codepoints.json for the CODEPOINTS, which that file DERIVES by three agreeing methods and marks as derived. No row here asserts a certh value of its own. Encoding: ConScript Unicode Registry cirth, U+E080-U+E0FF. Faces: fonts/ArdaCSUR.woff2 ALONE -- a 16x16 bitmap at 64 units/em, and the only face this archive holds whose U+E080 block is actually cirth. See `font_finding`: TengwarTelcontar and Eldamar-1.1 both draw a TENGWA at every cirth codepoint they cover, so neither may stand in a cirth font stack.

basis.mode-of-its-own-tongue: Eldamo records this form as Quenya, and the classical mode is the mode Appendix E assigns to Quenya. The letters are Tolkien's; the setting of this name in them is the archive's. [I-H]
basis.APPLIED: RETIRED BY HIS RULING C896, 6 September 2026, and kept here so a reader of an older copy can still find out what it meant. It marked a name Eldamo does not record as Quenya that had been set in the classical Quenya mode anyway -- 534 routes on the last build before C896. Those names now take the General Use instead, which is a mode their consonants exist in. No row carries this basis any longer.
basis.general-use-outside-quenya: Eldamo does not record this form as Quenya, so it is set in the GENERAL USE, whose per-letter values site/arda_tengwar_mode_gu.json publishes under his ruling C896 -- read by hand off Appendix E's plate, [I-H] on every row, each citing the sentence of Appendix E it was read from. The series assignment used is the one Appendix E states for 'languages like the Westron'. The letters are Tolkien's; the setting of this name in them is the archive's. [I-H]
basis.general-use-applied-to-an-elvish-name: The same mode and the same letters, and the difference is DECLARED rather than hidden. DTS 58 states the general use is 'applicable to both S[indarin] and Q[uenya]', so the mode fits; but Appendix E states the Series III/IV application for languages of the Westron type and for Quenya, and says in terms that it 'varied according to the requirements of different languages'. So for an Elvish name that is not Quenya the archive uses the Westron application and SAYS it is doing so. The one place it changes the reading is `c` before e, i or y, which Appendix E's own rule settles for the Elvish languages and not for others. [I-H]
basis.arrangement-of-its-subject: Appendix E's own use for the Cirth -- 'long used only for inscribing names and brief memorials upon wood or stone' -- in the arrangement this route's subject argues for: Erebor for Erebor and Dale, Moria for Dwarvish matter, Daeron otherwise. [I-H]
basis.arrangement-fallen-back: THE ARCHIVE'S OWN CHOICE, DECLARED, and marked [I-M] for it. The three arrangements are not one inventory -- Daeron has no `h` and no plain `y`, Erebor no unambiguous `s` -- so where the arrangement this route's subject argues for cannot spell the name, the name is set in one that can, in the fixed order daeron, moria, erebor. `arrangement_fallback` names the move and the letters that forced it. Tolkien did not inscribe this name in the arrangement fallen back to.

why.tengwar-no-value: A QUENYA name whose letters the classical Quenya mode has no cited value for. Since C896 this reaches only Quenya names: every other name goes to the General Use. Classical Quenya has no independent b, d, g, j, x or z, and no attestation will ever supply one -- in Quenya the voiced stops occur ONLY in the clusters nd, mb, ng, ngw, which is why Tolkien assigns ando, umbar and anga to the clusters and gives the stops no letters of their own. Nothing is guessed in its place.
why.tengwar-gu-no-value: A name outside Quenya whose spelling the General Use cannot route. The letters that stop it are named in `refused_letters` and the reason for each is in site/arda_tengwar_mode_gu.json under `routing.refused` -- and NOT ONE of them is a missing tengwa. `ch` is refused because Appendix E gives 3 = ch as in English CHURCH and 12 = the spirant of the k-series, and nothing in a written name says which it is; `x` because Appendix E writes it with an s-hook this archive holds no cited codepoint for; a bare `q` because Appendix E states no value for one; `c` before e, i or y in a name that is not Elvish because Appendix E's 'C has always the value of k' is stated of the ELVISH languages and an English-spelt name may sound an s there. Every one is a fact about the NAME, not about the plate.
why.cirth-no-certh: None of Appendix E's three arrangements carries a certh for the letters in `refused_letters`, and all three were tried. Those are Tolkien's tables and not this module's shortfall. A letter with no certh is refused and NAMED, never dropped silently and never replaced by something that looks close. `q` appears here because romanised Quenya writes `qu` where the Angerthas value is `kw`; joining the two is an orthographic rule and belongs in map/gen_edge_scripts.ORTHOGRAPHY, which verifies each rule's sentence in the corpus before applying it, not in this dataset.
why.sarati-refused: REFUSED, and not for want of a font or of permission. The archive holds 48/48 of the CSUR sarati block in fonts/ArdaCSUR.woff2, Bjorkman's outline face fonts/TirionSarati.woff2, and 66 value-labelled plates in site/sarati/ -- and NOTHING JOINS A SHAPE TO A SOUND. site/arda_sarati_keyboard.json refuses `sound -> glyph` and `sound -> codepoint` in its own words; reports/sarati_findings.json records zero assertable values; docs/sarati_values.md records that every value table in every reachable source is an IMAGE carrying no text. site/arda_sarati_tirion.json -- the shape-matching bridge that would supply it -- has never been written. A sarat can be DRAWN here and cannot be READ, so no name is set in it. CLAUDE.md section 6: a font is not a mapping.

conf_why.computed-not-attested: The CLAIM a row makes is that these glyphs are what the archive's own published letter tables produce for this name in the named mode -- NOT that Tolkien wrote it so. `rule_source` names the table a reader checks it against, and each of those files carries its own per-value markers.

keys.script_by_people: C80, 20 August 2026, the owner's ruling: the script is chosen by the subject's own people -- Elvish to the tengwar, Dwarvish and Moria matter to the cirth, the most ancient matter to the sarati. THAT RULING GOVERNS THE EDGE BAND (site/arda_edge_scripts.json), which carries one script per leaf. This dataset answers a different question -- how is the name written, in each script -- and gives every script the archive can honestly set. The ruling's choice is carried on every row so a reader and a guard can see which one it names, and it is never used here to suppress a script the archive can honestly write.
keys.transcription: the romanised form the scripts were set from: lower-cased, accents folded away, hyphens read as word joins (Khazad-dum is two words and the cirth have no sign for a hyphen)

orthography_applied.line: C has always the value of k even before e and i: celeb ‘silver’ should be
orthography_applied.why: LotR App E, the note on pronunciation. `c` is not a separate sound in these names and there is no certh for it; App E says outright which letter it is. The digraph `ch` still wins, because longest-match runs first.

orthography_applied.line: or Quenya, for ss: cf. Fëanorian 31. No. 39 was used for either i or y (conson-
orthography_applied.why: LotR App E, on the rearrangement of the Angerthas. The value string in arda_cirth.json reads `i (y)` and this is the sentence the parenthesis stands for.

orthography_applied.line: (1) the alteration in the values of 34, 35, 54 respectively to h, ’ (the clear or
orthography_applied.why: LotR App E, The Cirth, on the Angerthas Moria: 'the alteration in the values of 34, 35, 54 respectively to h, the clear or glottal beginning ... and s'. The same paragraph confirms it twice more -- 'the use of 17 as z, to go with 54 IN ITS VALUE s' -- and names where the arrangement is exhibited: 'This Angerthas Moria is represented in the tomb-inscription.' SCOPED TO MORIA, because the sentence is about the Dwarves' alteration: the older Angerthas keeps s at 34/35, which is why Daeron has one already, and the Erebor column's own `s*` is left dropped.
